presentation.label: TAPE SATURATION
presentation.summary: JClones TapeHead on the DSP: a small tape-style saturator with drive, trim and three tone colours.
presentation.overview: TapeHead runs the input through a two-state recursion whose corner frequency COLOR sets, drives both states into cubic smoothstep curves and adds a clipped feedback term. Low DRIVE gives gentle rounding and a slight tilt; high DRIVE flattens peaks and thickens the low end. It is a buffer-free insert, so it runs on FX1 or FX2 of every track. This is a source draft: it is not in the catalog or the firmware builder.
highlights: Port of JClones_TapeHead.jsfx, within 4.7e-4 of the float reference in a native render
DRIVE and TRIM as continuous 0-127 knobs over the JSFX ranges
COLOR: NORM, MED and BRGT corners at 2100, 3680 and 5000 Hz
No buffers: FX1 or FX2 on any track, 288 cycles/sample static
usage: Assign TAPEHEAD in FUNC + FX2 (or FX1) SETUP with LEVEL and YES. Defaults match the JSFX: DRIVE 36, TRIM 18 (-3 dB), COLOR NORM.
Raise DRIVE for more saturation; lower TRIM (towards 0) to bring the level back up, raise it to attenuate down to -21 dB.
Use COLOR for brightness: MED and BRGT move the recursion's corner up and let more top end through the saturator.

controls.name: DRIVE
controls.doc: Tape drive. 0-127 maps to the JSFX drive 1-10 (gain 0.8x to 8x into the curves); 36 is about the JSFX default 3.5.

controls.name: TRIM
controls.doc: Output trim. 0 is 0 dB, 127 is -21 dB; 18 is the JSFX default -3 dB. Higher values are quieter.

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Corner frequency of the recursion: NORM 2100 Hz, MED 3680 Hz, BRGT 5000 Hz.

limitations: Draft only: not in the catalog, configurator or firmware builder until qualification and owner review are complete.
The JSFX Clip switch is not exposed. Clip is always on (the JSFX default), because Q1.23 cannot carry the unclipped mode.
Corner frequencies assume 44.1 kHz, the rate every Octamod effect assumes.

This revision changes the sound of the octabam build heard on 12 Sep 2026: three defects were fixed (see TESTING.md). The OCTABAM2 test image of this revision was flashed and listened to on 2 Oct 2026; it has not been stress-tested.
Effect ID 0x1f, priority 17 and layout letter 4 were checked free against the eleven Octamod modules only.

storage.label: DSP program
storage.display: 416 words P, 31 words X per instance, no buffer
storage.conditions: Composed build report (both payloads place 416 words in the donor region). State and scratch use 31 words of the instance's own r7 block; no allocator buffer, no Y memory. SPRING REV: 1,063 words plus the 16,384-word FX2 instance buffer.

processing.label: DSP estimate
processing.conditions: tools/build/cycle_count.py static word count, the same at every setting. benchmark.py, executed instructions: 268/sample for one instance (SPRING REV 262); four per core worst 17,616 per 16-sample block (SPRING REV 20,376). Not a hardware load figure.

impact.conditions: One active instance at any setting (no stage is skipped, COLOR only swaps constants); the static count covers the worst case.

cpu.rationale: No ColdFire code: the module is a DSP insert with a cloned menu descriptor. The ColdFire only forwards three page-1 parameter values, as for any effect.

dsp.rationale: 288 cycles/sample per instance by the static counter. benchmark.py: one instance executes 2% more than stock SPRING REV (4,287 vs 4,186 instructions per block); four per core peak 14% lower (17,616 vs 20,376) because Spring's costlier types and splits are absent.

memory.rationale: 416 words of DSP program per payload and 31 words of state in each instance's existing r7 block. No allocator buffer, tables or Y memory, where SPRING REV takes 1,063 words and a 16,384-word instance buffer.

tests.summary: verify.py renders the assembled module in dsp_host against the float JSFX (peak error 4.7e-4); the composed hardware-test image renders it within 3.9e-5 of the JSFX at defaults. Benchmarked against stock SPRING REV with benchmark.py. Menu, init-register and replace gates pass; MKII emulator LCD captures included. Flashed by the author on 2 Oct 2026 (OCTABAM2 test image) and reported working; no hardware stress test.
gates: Worst-case cycles under parameter modulation on hardware
Real hardware stress project: eight audio tracks, at least 60 minutes

access.location: FUNC + FX1 or FUNC + FX2 SETUP on an audio track: the effect chooser (LEVEL selects, YES assigns). DRIVE, TRIM and COLOR are on the FX main page.
steps: Select an audio track that plays a sample, transport stopped or running.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 (or FX1) to open its SETUP. Turn LEVEL to TAPEHEAD and press YES to assign it.
Press FX2 (or FX1) to show the main page: DRIVE, TRIM and COLOR. The SETUP page has no TapeHead controls.
Verified on the MKII panel of the emulator with the hardware test image; not yet on a unit.
